details:
These silent heroes, space equipments, which enabled humanity to gain invaluable knowledge about space and the universe, never deserve to be forgotten, even though they are lost in the depths of space. In this project, we aimed to convey to younger generations, in a story-driven and sustainable format, that spacecraft are not merely heaps of metal; on the contrary, each one is a monument carrying the silent legacy of science. Our project is not just a presentation; it is an open-access educational ecosystem that teachers can actively use in their lessons during Space Week, where students transform from passive listeners into co-authors of stories. In this initiative, which specifically aims to spark a love for science and a sense of curiosity among secondary school students, we designed our monthly 'TRIN' digital magazine, our interactive Padlet page that builds a living inter-school interaction network, and our 3D virtual museum—whose QR code we will also feature in our magazine—as a complementary, integrated structure. Thanks to this sustainable ecosystem, students become a part of these stories with their own imagination while discovering the engineering marvels behind abandoned spacecraft. We reunite these silent explorers of the past with today's young minds; because they may be abandoned, but they will never be forgotten.

Although the pages of our magazine end here, our journey of discovery continues. Space-themed puzzles, analytical activities, and scientific experiments await our readers in the magazine we have designed. Furthermore, to complete ALSEP’s unfinishedstory with their own imagination, we direct them to our interactive Padlet platform—accessible via the QR code in our TRINmagazine—where we include them in ourstory every month while developing their storytelling and writing skills. You can access our TRIN magazine through the links we added.
